data.gender_notes: Barsha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Barsha is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Vrshabha’, which means rain, monsoon, or a cloudburst. This name is often used to describe the arrival of the monsoon season or the onset of rains. The name Barsha carries the meaning “Rain, Monsoon” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Barsha usually hope their child will grow to embody rain, monsoon and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Barsha holds special significance for various Indian cultures. In Hinduism, the monsoon season is considered auspicious as it symbolizes the renewal of life and nature. This is reflected in various festivals and rituals, such as the Ruru-Sankramana festival, which is celebrated in Manipur during the first raindrop. The arrival of rains is also believed to indicate the beginning of the agricultural cycle.
data.spiritual_significance: However, beyond its literal meaning of rain or monsoon, Barsha has deeper spiritual significance in Hinduism. It represents transformation and the renewal of life. This is symbolized by the cleansing and purifying power of the rains. Barsha is also associated with Lord Indra, the god of rain in Hindu mythology. The name is believed to bring blessings of abundance, new beginnings, and prosperity.
